editorial_principles: Replaceability = 'if swapped today, would it work?' — capability × commercial availability × barrier frictions

ISCO-08 canonical codes for all 481 occupations, 3 source families per common-titles list, 5,655 Phase-4 task decompositions, blind-calibrated 2026 replaceability scores with 3-scorer reconciliation, empirically-calibrated replacement formula with barrier-type multipliers, 2026-2041 capability trajectories under three scenarios, and Phase 8 barrier notes with 101 unique evidence domains.
changes: 481 occupations (vs v3.2 388) — ISCO-08 canonical codes + Phase 2 specialized splits
635 labor records (vs v3.2 608) — Phase 3 occupation-up ILOSTAT/GGDC/historical
77 timeline events (vs v3.2 57) — Phase 9 with primary-source citations
2026 replaceability scores — new per Phase 5 (blind calibrator + 3 scorers + reconciler)
Replacement formula re-calibrated — Phase 6 fit to 7 historical cases + Anthropic Economic Index
2026-2041 capability trajectories under three scenarios — Phase 7
Barrier notes rewritten where weak — Phase 8 (targeted-rewrite pass with evidence URLs)
Common titles: 3,838 unique across 481 occupations from O*NET + BLS + live LinkedIn
Display territory assignments curated — 104 displays (13 modern territories × 8 each)

metadata.labor_coverage_note: Phase 3 labor records are decadal for most modern territories post-1900 (not annual) because ILOSTAT/GGDC underlying sources are decadal-anchored pre-1991. Annual data exists 1991-2025 from ILOSTAT. This is a known, accepted design per Phase 3 signoff — not a data gap.
metadata.capability_trajectories_summary_note: Post Phase 11 parallel-shift values. Mid band = min(A_mid, B_mid) from two Phase 7 forecasters, then shifted by the 2026 recalibration delta per vector so the 2026 anchor equals the recalibrated capability_vectors_2026 value.

scenarios_shipped.note: v5.0 ships the moderate (mid) scenario as the editorially-reviewed display. Low and high band values are preserved in every occupation record for audit-trail purposes, but are produced deterministically from the Phase 7 capability-trajectory low/high curves applied against Phase 4 task difficulties — they were not individually reviewed at the occupation level. Illustrative examples (e.g., r30_high=100 for preschool educators) reflect mechanical saturation when Phi_U high=0.67 crosses Phi_U task thresholds of 0.55-0.60, not an editorial judgement. Re-examination of low/high band plausibility is deferred to v5.1.

phase12_historical_backfill.method: Honest-deployment-lens capability trajectory reconciled from GPT-5.4 + Opus 4.7 parallel instances, applied via logistic crossover (k=8) to current task decompositions, employment-weighted per territory using current within-territory weights.
phase12_historical_backfill.note: Pre-2015 values reflect what share of today's labor (per current task decompositions) would have been technically replaceable at each historical year's capability values. Actual historical replacement was lower due to economic, preference, and regulatory barriers — which is the model's core replaceability-vs-replacement distinction.

replaceability_computation.formula: r(occ, year) = 100 * Σ time_weight × 1/(1+exp(-8·(capability[vec][year] − task.difficulty))) / Σ time_weight
replaceability_computation.reason: Replaces Phase 5 calibrator holistic output and Phase 7 calibrator-propagated projections with bottom-up task-math. Resolves specification-implementation gap where methodology described task-math but data carried calibrator judgments. Logistic k=8 matches Phase 12 historical backfill discipline and gives partial credit as capability approaches task difficulty — the correct shape when capability is below task thresholds.
replaceability_computation.downstream_effects: displacement_*_moderate recomputed via Phase 6 formula fed with new task-math r values; barrier assignments, employment weights, task decompositions, capability trajectories unchanged

technology_events.impact_description: James Watt patented the separate condenser steam-engine improvement, reducing fuel consumption and enabling broader industrial use of stationary steam power.
technology_events.citation: Watt, J. (1769). Specification for patent No. 913: Method of lessening the consumption of steam and fuel in fire engines.

technology_events.impact_description: James Hargreaves' multi-spindle spinning frame was recorded in the patent context by 1770, marking a major labor-saving textile invention that concentrated yarn production around machines.
technology_events.citation: Science Museum Group. (n.d.). Replica of Hargreaves' spinning jenny.

technology_events.impact_description: Edmund Cartwright's power loom mechanized weaving, extending textile automation from spinning into cloth production and reshaping factory labor demand.
technology_events.citation: Encyclopaedia Britannica. (n.d.). Power loom.

technology_events.impact_description: Andrew Meikle's threshing-machine work mechanized separation of grain from stalks, replacing seasonal hand-flail labor with a farm machine platform later adopted across Britain.
technology_events.citation: DMG-Lib. (n.d.). Andrew Meikle biography.

technology_events.impact_description: Eli Whitney's cotton gin patent mechanized cotton-seed separation, sharply reducing processing labor while intensifying plantation cotton production.
technology_events.citation: National Archives. (n.d.). Patent for cotton gin.

technology_events.impact_description: Whitney's federal musket contract made interchangeable-parts manufacturing a government-backed production program, even though full interchangeability matured later.
technology_events.citation: Eli Whitney arms manufacturing contract (1798), 10,000 muskets for the U.S. government; widely documented across National Archives and scholarly histories.
technology_events.verifier_note: Source URL corrected per Checkpoint 9 verifier. Historical event confirmed real; secondary-source citation pending primary-archive link.

technology_events.impact_description: Jacquard's punched-card loom automated complex textile patterns and created a durable control-media lineage for later computing and industrial automation.
technology_events.citation: Smithsonian Institution. (n.d.). Punch cards.

technology_events.impact_description: The Stockton and Darlington Railway opened as an early public steam railway, demonstrating mechanized freight and passenger transport at commercial scale.
technology_events.citation: Darlington Borough Council. (n.d.). Stockton and Darlington Railway.

technology_events.impact_description: An 1841 primary-school blackboard manual documents the classroom shift toward reusable shared visual instruction, a low-cost teaching medium that scaled group pedagogy.
technology_events.citation: Library of Congress. (n.d.). The blackboard in the primary school.

technology_events.impact_description: Morse's Washington-to-Baltimore message proved practical long-distance electrical communication, cutting information labor from days of travel to near-instant signaling.
technology_events.citation: Library of Congress. (n.d.). What hath God wrought!

technology_events.impact_description: Henry Bessemer's steelmaking patent introduced a process that lowered steel costs and enabled rail, bridge, machine, and construction expansion.
technology_events.citation: Bessemer, H. (1856). Improvement in the manufacture of iron and steel. U.S. Patent No. 16,082.

technology_events.impact_description: The joining of the Union Pacific and Central Pacific railroads at Promontory linked US coasts by rail, reorganizing freight, migration, and national labor markets.
technology_events.citation: National Park Service. (n.d.). The last spike: history at a glance.

technology_events.impact_description: Commercial sale of the Sholes & Glidden typewriter mechanized office writing and helped create large clerical labor markets centered on typed documents.
technology_events.citation: The Henry Ford. (n.d.). Sholes & Glidden typewriter.

technology_events.impact_description: Alexander Graham Bell's telephone patent established a practical electrical speech-transmission system, eventually displacing telegraphy for many coordination tasks.
technology_events.citation: Bell, A. G. (1876). Improvement in telegraphy. U.S. Patent No. 174,465.

technology_events.impact_description: Edison's practical electric-lamp patent anchored commercial lighting systems that extended productive hours and reshaped factories, offices, streets, and homes.
technology_events.citation: Edison, T. A. (1880). Electric lamp. U.S. Patent No. 223,898.

technology_events.impact_description: The Audion triode enabled signal amplification and switching, becoming a foundation for radio, telephony, electronic control, and early computing.
technology_events.citation: Smithsonian National Museum of American History. (n.d.). De Forest Audion triode vacuum tube.

technology_events.impact_description: Ford's moving assembly line reorganized automobile production around paced, specialized work, sharply reducing assembly time and redefining industrial labor.
technology_events.citation: Ford Motor Company. (n.d.). Moving assembly line.

technology_events.impact_description: KDKA's election-night broadcast showed radio as a mass communication service, opening a new industry for live news, entertainment, and advertising labor.
technology_events.citation: CBS Pittsburgh. (2020). KDKA's historic broadcast.

technology_events.impact_description: John Logie Baird's 1925-1926 experimental apparatus produced recognizable television images, marking a verifiable step toward broadcast visual media.
technology_events.citation: Science Museum Group. (n.d.). John Logie Baird's original experimental television apparatus, 1925-1926.

technology_events.impact_description: Turing's computability paper formalized the abstract machine model that underpins programmable computing and later automated information work.
technology_events.citation: Turing, A. M. (1937). On computable numbers, with an application to the Entscheidungsproblem. Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society.

technology_events.impact_description: Chester Carlson's xerographic process made dry photocopying possible, eventually automating office document reproduction at massive scale.
technology_events.citation: Xerox. (n.d.). Chester Carlson and xerography.

technology_events.impact_description: Britain's Chain Home radar network fed Fighter Command during the Battle of Britain, linking sensing, filtering, and command decisions in an early cybernetic defense system.
technology_events.citation: Royal Air Force. (n.d.). Battle of Britain.

technology_events.impact_description: ENIAC's public announcement demonstrated a general-purpose electronic computer able to automate large numerical calculations for military and scientific work.
technology_events.citation: University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science. (n.d.). ENIAC.

technology_events.impact_description: The Speedee Service System standardized fast-food preparation into specialized, repeatable tasks, a service-sector analogue of assembly-line labor design.
technology_events.citation: McDonald's Corporation. (n.d.). Our history.

technology_events.impact_description: NIST's SEAC became an operational stored-program electronic computer, providing federal computation capacity for scientific and standards work.
technology_events.citation: National Institute of Standards and Technology. (n.d.). SEAC - Standards Eastern Automatic Computer.

technology_events.event_name: American Airlines and IBM Sign SABRE Development Agreement
technology_events.impact_description: American Airlines and IBM's SABRE collaboration began automating airline reservations, a major step in transaction processing and real-time business data systems. Formal IBM–American Airlines development agreement signed 1957; experimental system online 1960; full operations 1964.
technology_events.citation: IBM. (n.d.). SABRE.
technology_events.verifier_note: Year corrected 1953→1957 per Checkpoint 9 verifier. 1953 was chance executive meeting; 1957 was formal collaboration start.

technology_events.impact_description: Unimate's factory installation at General Motors brought programmable industrial robots into production work, starting a new automation category for hazardous repetitive tasks.
technology_events.citation: International Federation of Robotics. (n.d.). History of industrial robots.

technology_events.impact_description: Intel's 4004 integrated a programmable central processor onto a chip, enabling smaller, cheaper, and more widely embedded computation.
technology_events.citation: Intel. (n.d.). The story of the Intel 4004.

technology_events.impact_description: The IBM PC gave businesses a standardized personal-computing platform, accelerating office software, spreadsheets, and distributed information work.
technology_events.citation: IBM. (n.d.). The IBM personal computer.

technology_events.impact_description: Tim Berners-Lee's web proposal at CERN laid out linked hypertext over networks, creating the architecture for browser-based digital work and information distribution.
technology_events.citation: CERN. (n.d.). The birth of the web.

technology_events.impact_description: Amazon opened on the web in July 1995, demonstrating large-scale online retail and reshaping warehousing, logistics, and customer-service labor.
technology_events.citation: Amazon. (1995, October 4). World's Largest Bookseller Opens on the Web.

technology_events.impact_description: The Google search architecture turned link analysis into scalable web ranking, creating a new organizing layer for online knowledge and advertising work.
technology_events.citation: Brin, S., & Page, L. (1998). The anatomy of a large-scale hypertextual web search engine.

technology_events.event_name: da Vinci Surgical System Receives FDA Clearance
technology_events.impact_description: FDA clearance and clinical rollout of the da Vinci system made robotic-assisted surgery a regulated medical deployment rather than a laboratory prototype.
technology_events.citation: Intuitive. (n.d.). Company history.

technology_events.impact_description: Amazon Mechanical Turk exposed human microtasks through an API, creating a market for on-demand distributed digital labor used by software systems.
technology_events.citation: Amazon Web Services. (2005, November 2). Announcing Amazon Mechanical Turk.

technology_events.event_name: Amazon S3 Launches AWS Cloud Storage
technology_events.impact_description: Amazon S3 launched as a scalable web service for object storage, turning data infrastructure into programmable, metered cloud capacity.
technology_events.citation: Amazon. (2006, March 14). Amazon Web Services launches.

technology_events.impact_description: Apple's iPhone combined phone, internet communicator, and touchscreen computer, shifting digital work and services toward mobile platforms.
technology_events.citation: Apple. (2007, January 9). Apple reinvents the phone with iPhone.

technology_events.impact_description: The App Store created a mass software marketplace for mobile devices, changing developer labor, distribution, and consumer-service workflows.
technology_events.citation: Apple. (2008, July 14). iPhone App Store downloads top 10 million in first weekend.

technology_events.impact_description: AlexNet's ImageNet result showed deep convolutional neural networks could outperform prior computer-vision pipelines, catalyzing modern deep learning adoption.
technology_events.citation: Krizhevsky, A., Sutskever, I., & Hinton, G. E. (2012). ImageNet classification with deep convolutional neural networks. NeurIPS.

technology_events.impact_description: Deep recurrent neural networks with LSTM-style sequence modeling improved speech recognition, advancing automated transcription and voice interfaces.
technology_events.citation: Graves, A., Mohamed, A., & Hinton, G. (2013). Speech recognition with deep recurrent neural networks. arXiv.

technology_events.impact_description: GANs introduced a two-network training method that made high-quality generative modeling a central AI research path for images, media, and simulation.
technology_events.citation: Goodfellow, I., et al. (2014). Generative adversarial nets. NeurIPS.

technology_events.impact_description: AlphaGo's match victory over Lee Sedol demonstrated superhuman performance in Go and popularized deep reinforcement learning as a frontier AI method.
technology_events.citation: Google DeepMind. (2016). AlphaGo: The story so far.

technology_events.event_name: Amazon Go Opens to the Public
technology_events.impact_description: Amazon Go's public cashierless store deployed computer vision and sensor fusion in retail, automating checkout work in a live service environment.
technology_events.citation: Amazon. (2018). The big picture.

technology_events.impact_description: OpenAI released GPT-2 as a large transformer language model, showing coherent long-form text generation and raising deployment-governance questions.
technology_events.citation: OpenAI. (2019, February 14). Better language models and their implications.

technology_events.impact_description: AlphaFold's CASP14 performance made protein-structure prediction accurate enough to alter biological research workflows and accelerate drug-discovery pipelines.
technology_events.citation: Google DeepMind. (2020). AlphaFold: a solution to a 50-year-old grand challenge in biology.

technology_events.event_name: China Robot Density Reaches 246 per 10,000 Workers
technology_events.impact_description: IFR World Robotics 2021 reports China at 246 robots per 10,000 manufacturing workers in 2020, up from 49 in 2015 — a five-fold increase in five years, placing China ninth globally.
technology_events.citation: International Federation of Robotics. (2020). Robot density nearly doubled globally.
technology_events.verifier_note: Figure corrected per Checkpoint 9 verifier. 2019/140 figure not in cited source; substituted IFR-verified 2020/246 anchor.

technology_events.impact_description: GPT-3 demonstrated few-shot language learning at large scale, making prompt-based general-purpose text generation a practical research and product direction.
technology_events.citation: Brown, T. B., et al. (2020). Language models are few-shot learners. arXiv.

technology_events.event_name: OpenAI Codex and GitHub Copilot Launch
technology_events.impact_description: Codex and Copilot brought transformer code generation into developer workflows, making AI pair-programming a mainstream labor augmentation pattern.
technology_events.citation: OpenAI. (2021, August 10). OpenAI Codex.

technology_events.impact_description: ChatGPT's public release made conversational generative AI broadly accessible, accelerating adoption across writing, support, tutoring, coding, and knowledge work.
technology_events.citation: OpenAI. (2022, November 30). Introducing ChatGPT.

technology_events.impact_description: Stable Diffusion's public release made text-to-image generation widely available and locally runnable, transforming creative production and asset workflows.
technology_events.citation: Stability AI. (2022, August 22). Stable Diffusion public release.

technology_events.impact_description: DALL-E 3's ChatGPT integration shifted image generation toward conversational prompting and made AI art direction easier for non-specialists.
technology_events.citation: OpenAI. (2023, September 20). DALL-E 3.

technology_events.impact_description: Google launched Gemini as a multimodal AI model family, intensifying frontier competition around integrated text, code, image, and reasoning capabilities.
technology_events.citation: Google. (2023, December 6). Introducing Gemini.

technology_events.impact_description: AlphaFold 3 extended AI structure prediction from proteins toward biomolecular interactions, broadening automation potential in biology and drug discovery.
technology_events.citation: Abramson, J., Adler, J., Dunger, J., et al. (2024). Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3. Nature.

technology_events.impact_description: Claude 3.5 Sonnet improved frontier coding, writing, and reasoning performance at lower latency and cost, expanding enterprise AI assistant use cases.
technology_events.citation: Anthropic. (2024, June 20). Claude 3.5 Sonnet.

technology_events.impact_description: Anthropic released a computer-use beta that let Claude operate user interfaces through screenshots and actions, a key step toward general desktop agents.
technology_events.citation: Anthropic. (2024, October 22). Introducing computer use, a new Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Claude 3.5 Haiku.

technology_events.impact_description: Cognition previewed Devin as an autonomous software-engineering agent, signaling a shift from code completion toward multi-step agentic development workflows.
technology_events.citation: Cognition. (2024, March 12). Introducing Devin.

technology_events.event_name: EU AI Act Enters into Force
technology_events.impact_description: The EU AI Act entered into force, creating a risk-based legal framework for AI development and deployment that affects employers, vendors, and public agencies.
technology_events.citation: European Commission. (2024, August 1). AI Act enters into force.

technology_events.impact_description: GPT-4o introduced faster native multimodal interaction across text, audio, and vision, pushing AI assistants toward real-time conversational work.
technology_events.citation: OpenAI. (2024, May 13). Hello GPT-4o.

technology_events.impact_description: NVIDIA announced Blackwell, an AI-compute platform designed for trillion-parameter generative models, reinforcing specialized infrastructure as a labor-market bottleneck.
technology_events.citation: NVIDIA. (2024, March 18). NVIDIA Blackwell Platform arrives to power a new era of computing.

technology_events.impact_description: OpenAI o1-preview foregrounded inference-time reasoning for hard math, science, and coding tasks, marking a public turn toward reasoning-specialized frontier models.
technology_events.citation: OpenAI. (2024, September 12). Introducing OpenAI o1-preview.

technology_events.impact_description: Unitree's G1 product announcement showed sub-enterprise humanoid hardware moving into public commercial availability, though broad labor deployment remained early.
technology_events.citation: Unitree Robotics. (n.d.). Unitree G1.

technology_events.event_name: Waymo One Opens to Everyone in San Francisco
technology_events.impact_description: Waymo removed the San Francisco waitlist, making fully autonomous ride-hailing available citywide to the public and scaling driverless transport as a service.
technology_events.citation: Waymo. (2024, June 25). Waymo One is now open to everyone in San Francisco.

technology_events.impact_description: FDA clearance of Intuitive's da Vinci 5 advanced robotic surgery into a new regulated generation with improved sensing and surgeon-assistance capabilities.
technology_events.citation: Intuitive Surgical. (2024, March 14). Intuitive announces FDA clearance of fifth-generation robotic system, da Vinci 5.

technology_events.impact_description: Anthropic released Claude 4, emphasizing coding, agentic search, and long-running development tasks through Claude Code.
technology_events.citation: Anthropic. (2025, May 22). Introducing Claude 4.

technology_events.impact_description: Claude Opus 4.5 advanced coding, agents, computer use, spreadsheets, and long-horizon tasks, making Opus-level capability cheaper and more deployable.
technology_events.citation: Anthropic. (2025, November 24). Introducing Claude Opus 4.5.

technology_events.impact_description: Claude Sonnet 4.5 improved coding, agent building, computer use, reasoning, and math, strengthening frontier AI support for complex digital work.
technology_events.citation: Anthropic. (2025, September 29). Introducing Claude Sonnet 4.5.

technology_events.impact_description: EU general-purpose AI model obligations started applying, adding transparency, copyright, documentation, and systemic-risk duties for model providers.
technology_events.citation: European Commission. (2025, August 1). EU rules on general-purpose AI models start to apply.

technology_events.event_name: FDA AI Medical Device Authorizations Surge
technology_events.impact_description: FDA's public AI/ML-enabled device list documented hundreds of authorized medical AI devices, showing regulated clinical AI moving beyond isolated pilots.
technology_events.citation: U.S. Food and Drug Administration. (n.d.). Artificial intelligence and machine learning-enabled medical devices.

technology_events.impact_description: OpenAI released GPT-5 in its API platform, with strong coding and agentic-task performance that made frontier models more directly useful for professional workflows.
technology_events.citation: OpenAI. (2025, August 7). Introducing GPT-5 for developers.

technology_events.impact_description: GPT-5-Codex specialized GPT-5 for long-running agentic software engineering, including code review and multi-hour independent development tasks.
technology_events.citation: OpenAI. (2025, September 15). Introducing upgrades to Codex.

technology_events.impact_description: GPT-5.1 introduced adaptive reasoning and no-reasoning modes, improving the speed-cost-quality tradeoff for agentic and coding workloads.
technology_events.citation: OpenAI. (2025, November 13). Introducing GPT-5.1 for developers.

technology_events.impact_description: GPT-5.2 improved professional knowledge-work, tool-use, long-context, and software-engineering benchmarks, including GDPval and SWE-bench style tasks.
technology_events.citation: OpenAI. (2025, December 11). Introducing GPT-5.2.

technology_events.impact_description: GPT-5.2-Codex advanced agentic coding and defensive cybersecurity capabilities for professional software engineering workflows.
technology_events.citation: OpenAI. (2025, December 18). Introducing GPT-5.2-Codex.

technology_events.event_name: METR AI Task Time Horizon Benchmark
technology_events.impact_description: METR's time-horizon benchmark measured how long AI agents can autonomously complete real tasks, providing a labor-relevant capability metric beyond static exams.
technology_events.citation: METR. (2025, March 19). Measuring AI ability to complete long tasks.

technology_events.impact_description: Meta released Llama 4 as a natively multimodal open-weight model family, keeping frontier-adjacent capabilities accessible outside closed API platforms.
technology_events.citation: Meta AI. (2025). The Llama 4 herd: The beginning of a new era of natively multimodal AI innovation.

technology_events.impact_description: OpenAI released o3 and o4-mini as reasoning models able to combine tools inside ChatGPT, advancing agentic problem solving across coding, math, science, and visual tasks.
technology_events.citation: OpenAI. (2025, April 16). Introducing OpenAI o3 and o4-mini.

technology_events.event_name: Anthropic Economic Index Learning Curves Report
technology_events.impact_description: Anthropic's 2026 Economic Index report used privacy-preserving Claude usage telemetry to track task-level augmentation and automation patterns across the economy.
technology_events.citation: Massenkoff, M., Lyubich, E., McCrory, P., Appel, R., & Heller, R. (2026, March 24). Anthropic Economic Index report: Learning curves.

technology_events.impact_description: GPT-5.3-Codex expanded Codex across professional computer work with faster frontier agentic coding, research, tool use, and complex execution.
technology_events.citation: OpenAI. (2026, February 5). Introducing GPT-5.3-Codex.

technology_events.impact_description: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5, the first public Mythos-class frontier model, with Claude Mythos 5 available under controlled access for vetted cybersecurity and infrastructure work.
technology_events.citation: Anthropic. (2026, June 9). Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5.

technology_events.impact_description: Claude Sonnet 5 brought near-Opus agentic capability, tool use, and a 1M-token context to Anthropic's default consumer and developer tier at commodity pricing.
technology_events.citation: Anthropic. (2026, June 30). Introducing Claude Sonnet 5.

technology_events.impact_description: OpenAI released the GPT-5.6 family (Luna, Terra, Sol) after a staged government safety review, alongside ChatGPT Work, a workspace agent built to complete multi-step projects and deliver finished documents, spreadsheets, and apps.
technology_events.citation: OpenAI. (2026, July 9). GPT-5.6: Frontier intelligence that scales with your ambition.

technology_events.impact_description: Claude Opus 5 set new state-of-the-art results on knowledge-work and coding evaluations, delivering near-frontier capability at half frontier price with user-selectable effort.
technology_events.citation: Anthropic. (2026, July 24). Introducing Claude Opus 5.

technology_events.impact_description: SpaceXAI released Grok 4.5, an Opus-class model focused on coding and agentic work, trained with Cursor session data and priced aggressively against frontier rivals.

technology_events.event_name: Figure 03 Enters Production Logistics at BMW Spartanburg
technology_events.impact_description: After an 11-month Figure 02 pilot that supported production of over 30,000 BMW X3 vehicles, BMW deployed Figure 03 humanoids for parts sequencing in Spartanburg production logistics, with expansion planned across tasks and plants.
technology_events.citation: BMW Group. (2026, June 25). BMW Group advances the use of physical AI in production with Figure 03 project in Spartanburg.

technology_events.event_name: EU Digital Omnibus Delays High-Risk AI Rules as GPAI Enforcement Begins
technology_events.impact_description: The EU Digital Omnibus (Regulation 2026/1744) postponed Annex III high-risk AI obligations to December 2027, while GPAI penalty enforcement and Article 50 transparency duties took effect on 2 August 2026.
technology_events.citation: Gibson Dunn. (2026). EU AI Act Omnibus Agreement — Postponed high-risk deadlines and other key changes.

technology_events.event_name: Aurora Expands Driverless Trucking to 10 Commercial Routes
technology_events.impact_description: Aurora's second-generation driverless trucks entered commercial freight service across 10 US routes, with nearly 440,000 driverless miles completed and manufacturing targeting 1,000 trucks per year.
technology_events.citation: ACT News. (2026, July 22). Aurora's second-generation driverless trucks enter commercial service on 10 U.S. routes.

technology_events.impact_description: Anthropic's Cadences report combined usage telemetry with worker surveys, finding automation's share of Claude conversations still rising slowly while augmentation remains the dominant pattern of AI-assisted work.
technology_events.citation: Massenkoff, M., Lyubich, E., Sacher, S., Hitzig, Z., Zhang, S., Heller, R., & McCrory, P. (2026, June 26). Anthropic Economic Index report: Cadences.

technology_events.event_name: Agility Digit Deployed at GXO in First Commercial Humanoid RaaS
technology_events.impact_description: Agility Robotics' Digit began paid work at a GXO logistics facility near Atlanta under the industry's first Robots-as-a-Service humanoid agreement — the first humanoid robot formally deployed in revenue-generating operations.
technology_events.citation: Agility Robotics. (2024, June 5). GXO signs industry-first multi-year agreement with Agility Robotics.

technology_events.event_name: Amazon Deploys Its One-Millionth Warehouse Robot
technology_events.impact_description: Amazon deployed its one-millionth warehouse robot across more than 300 facilities and launched DeepFleet, a generative AI model coordinating fleet movement for a 10% travel-efficiency gain.
technology_events.citation: Amazon. (2025, July 1). Amazon launches a new AI foundation model to power its robotic fleet and deploys its 1 millionth robot.

technology_events.event_name: Tesla Launches Robotaxi Service in Austin
technology_events.impact_description: Tesla launched a limited robotaxi service in Austin with about 10 supervised Model Y vehicles, entering commercial autonomous ride-hailing alongside Waymo.
technology_events.citation: CNBC. (2025, June 22). Tesla robotaxi service launches in Austin.

technology_events.event_name: 1X NEO Consumer Home Humanoid Pre-Orders Open
technology_events.impact_description: 1X opened consumer pre-orders for NEO, a $20,000 (or $499/month) home humanoid for household chores with human-in-the-loop teleoperation backstop, with first deliveries in 2026.
technology_events.citation: The Robot Report. (2025, October 28). NEO humanoid designed for household use, available for preorder.

technology_events.impact_description: Google DeepMind released Gemini 3 Pro and Gemini 3 DeepThink across the Gemini app, AI Studio, and Vertex AI, returning Google to the reasoning and agentic frontier.
technology_events.citation: Google. (2025, November 18). Introducing Gemini 3 Pro for the Gemini app.

technology_events.impact_description: OpenAI released GPT-5.4 with a 33% reduction in factual errors versus GPT-5.2 and stronger computer-use and deep-research capability for professional work.
technology_events.citation: OpenAI. (2026, March 5). GPT-5.4 release.

technology_events.event_name: Jacobian Conjecture Disproved with Claude Fable 5
technology_events.impact_description: Number theorist Levent Alpöge, working with Anthropic's Claude Fable 5, produced a 216-character counterexample disproving the Jacobian conjecture, open since 1939 — verified by hand by mathematicians within a day.
technology_events.citation: Fortune, 'Mathematicians grapple with a very rapid and very unsettling change', July 21, 2026

technology_events.event_name: Amateur Solves 60-Year-Old Math Problem with GPT-5.4
technology_events.impact_description: A 23-year-old with no formal mathematical training, iterating with GPT-5.4, produced a proof of a 60-year-old open problem; Fields Medalist Terence Tao reviewed and endorsed the result within a day.
technology_events.citation: Slashdot, 'An Amateur Just Solved a 60-Year-Old Math Problem — by Asking AI', May 2, 2026
